description: Golden questions for the reference repository koajs/koa at the commit pinned in src/eval/reference-repository.ts (see samples/SOURCES.md). 'file' is the path inside the repository. Every quote is verbatim from that file; the code evaluation checks this when it fetches the repository.

questions.question: How does app.listen start the HTTP server?
questions.answer: It creates a Node http server from the app's callback() and calls listen on it.

questions.question: What happens when something that is not a function is passed to app.use?

expected.quote: if (typeof fn !== 'function') { throw new TypeError('middleware must be a function!') }

questions.answer: It throws a TypeError saying that middleware must be a function.

questions.question: What status code does a response have before any middleware has run?
questions.answer: 404; handleRequest sets it before running the middleware.

questions.question: Which function composes the middleware stack, and can it be replaced?
questions.answer: koa-compose by default; the compose option replaces it.

questions.question: How is the per-request context created from the application's context?
questions.answer: createContext derives it with Object.create(this.context), and does the same for request and response.

questions.question: When does the application attach its default error handler?
questions.answer: In callback(), only if no error listener has been registered.

questions.question: When does the application-level error handler skip logging an error?
questions.answer: When the status is 404 or the error is exposed (and also when the app is silent).

questions.question: How does Koa treat a response whose status never has a body, such as 204?
questions.answer: It clears the body and ends the response without sending one.

questions.question: How is an object body turned into the bytes that are sent?
questions.answer: It is serialised with JSON.stringify and its byte length becomes the Content-Length.

questions.question: Where does a HEAD response get its Content-Length from?
questions.answer: From the length of the response body, when it is an integer and the header is not already set.

questions.question: Which header holds the client address when the app runs behind a proxy, by default?
questions.answer: X-Forwarded-For, configurable with the proxyIpHeader option.

questions.question: How can code read the current request's context without it being passed in?
questions.answer: Through app.currentContext, which reads the AsyncLocalStorage store when asyncLocalStorage is enabled.

questions.question: Which HTTP error helpers does the application module export besides the class?
questions.answer: createHttpError, HttpError and isHttpError, taken from the http-errors package.

questions.question: How does ctx.throw create the error it throws?
questions.answer: It passes its arguments to http-errors' createError and throws the result.

questions.question: What is ctx.assert implemented with?
questions.answer: The http-assert package.

questions.question: What does the context error handler do with the headers already set before it replies with an error?
questions.answer: It removes all of them first, then sets only the headers carried by the error.

questions.question: When is the error's own message sent to the client instead of generic status text?
questions.answer: Only when err.expose is true; otherwise the status text such as Internal Server Error is sent.

questions.question: Where do the keys used for signed cookies come from?
questions.answer: From app.keys, which the Cookies object is created with.

questions.question: How are properties such as ctx.body and ctx.status forwarded to the response object?
questions.answer: Through the delegates package: the context delegates those accessors to its response.

questions.question: Which header does request.host look at first when proxy trust is enabled?
questions.answer: X-Forwarded-Host, before :authority and Host.

questions.question: How is the number of addresses read from the proxy header limited?
questions.answer: With maxIpsCount greater than zero only that many addresses, counted from the end, are kept.

questions.question: What does ctx.ip fall back to when there is no proxy address?
questions.answer: The socket's remote address, or an empty string.

questions.question: What does request.subdomains return when the host is an IP address?
questions.answer: An empty array.

questions.question: Which checks run when the response status is set?
questions.answer: The code must be an integer between 100 and 999; otherwise an assertion fails.

questions.question: How is the content type chosen when the body is a string?
questions.answer: If it starts with an angle bracket it is html, otherwise text, and only when no type was set yet.

questions.question: What happens to the status when the body is set to null and the status could have a body?
questions.answer: The status becomes 204 (No Content).

questions.question: Which status does redirect use if the current one is not a redirect status?
How does redirect prepare the address when the client accepts HTML?
questions.answer: It HTML-escapes the address before putting it in the body.

questions.question: When does Koa consider the response no longer writable?
questions.answer: When the underlying response has ended.

questions.question: What is the entry file of the package?
questions.answer: lib/application.js.

questions.question: What message does the default error handler send for an error that is not exposed and has status 500?

expected.quote: for the code 500 the message "Internal Server Error" will be used

questions.answer: The generated message "Internal Server Error".

questions.question: How are listeners for errors that reach the application registered?

expected.quote: Error event listeners can be specified with `app.on('error')`.

questions.answer: With app.on('error'); without one the default app.onerror logs the error.

questions.question: How can Koa's debugging output be turned on?
questions.answer: By running with NODE_DEBUG=koa*.

questions.question: How is a Koa application served over HTTP/2?
questions.answer: With http2.createSecureServer and the app's request handler.

questions.question: Which content type must a server-sent events response use?
questions.answer: text/event-stream.

questions.question: How does the example middleware record how long a request took?
questions.answer: It measures the time around await next() and sets it in the X-Response-Time header.

questions.question: Which header does it read for the host then?
questions.answer: X-Forwarded-Host.

history.content: How does Koa decide whether to trust proxy headers?
Through the app.proxy setting: when it is true, the proxy header fields are trusted.

questions.question: And which status does it use when none was set?

history.content: It sets the Location header to the encoded address and writes a short body that says where it redirects to.

questions.question: How does Koa implement WebSocket support?
questions.note: Nothing about WebSockets in the corpus.

questions.question: Which database drivers does Koa ship with?
How does Koa execute GraphQL queries?
How do I render Handlebars templates with Koa?
questions.note: No template engine in the corpus.

questions.question: How does Koa's built-in router match path parameters?
questions.note: Koa has no router; a near-miss for a routing question.

questions.question: Where is the built-in session store implemented?
How does Koa configure CORS headers by default?
